struck: A house that resold inside the city of Conway in the past year usually went for about $265,000.
use: A home that resold inside the city of Conway in the past year (a house or townhouse, not a condo unit) usually went for about $265,000.

struck: Large parts of Conway did not flood in Florence.
use: By the county's map, Florence's water did not reach large parts of Conway.

struck: After Matthew, the City of Conway used FEMA mitigation money to buy 86 flood-damaged buildings so they could be cleared. That is why some streets near the river have empty lots.
use: After Matthew, the City of Conway used FEMA mitigation grants to buy 86 buildings; after Hurricane Floyd in 1999 it bought 14. Land bought this way must stay open space.

struck: A flood policy usually starts 30 days after you buy it.
use: A new federal flood policy takes effect 30 days after the application and payment are complete, unless it is bought when a home loan is made.

struck: Conway is one of South Carolina's oldest towns.
use: Conway was laid out in 1732, as Kingston.
